query: What review signals predict negative Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: defect_type
per_column.rationale: The type of defect mentioned is a review signal external to the label; presence and category of defect plausibly predicts dissatisfaction without being a restatement of the label itself.

per_column.name: expectation_gap
per_column.rationale: Whether the product met/exceeded/fell below expectations is a distinct semantic signal carrying strong predictive value for satisfaction, yet not a mechanical restatement of the pos/neg label.

per_column.name: sentiment_intensity
per_column.rationale: A 1-5 sentiment/star-like intensity is essentially a graded restatement of the same satisfaction polarity the label encodes; label_pos is nearly a deterministic thresholding of this, so it leaks the focus rather than providing independent signal.

per_column.name: reviewer_use_context
per_column.rationale: The usage context (gift, child, professional, etc.) is an external variable that may correlate with satisfaction and is not derivable from the label; a legitimate, if weaker, predictor.

per_column.name: product_category_signal
per_column.rationale: Product category is a genuine external covariate that can carry predictive signal about satisfaction rates and is independent of the label.

judge.rationale: Four of five added columns (defect_type, expectation_gap, reviewer_use_context, product_category_signal) are legitimate external predictors extracted from review text, with defect_type and expectation_gap carrying the strongest genuine signal about dissatisfaction. However, sentiment_intensity is effectively a graded restatement of the satisfaction polarity itself and constitutes leakage of the focus variable. As a set the columns give solid, non-trivial predictive leverage beyond the raw text, but the presence of a leaky feature and the weaker signal of context/category caps the overall utility.
